tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file outside the working directory, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

schema.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
schema.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

content.text:
## Lavie's Hypothetical August Salary — 18% Revenue + 4,000,000 Base

I pulled this directly from the Soul Pilates production database (studionexis-soul, `SoulPilates.API`/MongoDB) — read-only, no data touched.

**Lavie's August 2026 activity:**
- 42 classes scheduled, 32 with at least one paying attendee (27 group, 5 private) — matches the studio's existing payroll run for the month
- 50 total billable attendances (all `CountsTowardsCommission: true`, consistent with how the app already treats cancellations/no-shows as revenue-earning)

**Class revenue reconstruction** (VND):
| Source | Attendances | Revenue |
|---|---|---|
| Package-credit bookings (amortized via each client's `FractionalValuePerClass`) | 32 | 13,977,500 |
| Direct pay-at-studio bookings (`AmountPaid`) | 18 | 9,550,000 |
| **Total class revenue** | 50 | **23,527,500** |

**Applying your hypothetical structure:**
- 18% × 23,527,500 = **4,234,950**
- \+ base salary **4,000,000**
- = **Total: 8,234,950 VND**

**For comparison**, her actual August pay under the current `FIXED_HEADCOUNT` model was **6,250,000 VND** (27 group classes = 5,125,000 + 5 private = 1,125,000). The proposed 18%+base structure would pay her **~1,984,950 VND more (+31.8%)** for the same August workload.

Note on methodology: "class revenue" isn't a field the app stores directly for headcount-model instructors (that's only computed for the owner's studio-wide REVENUE_SPLIT model), so I reconstructed it per-class using the same package-amortization value (`FractionalValuePerClass`) the app already computes per client package, plus actual direct payments — this is the most faithful proxy for "money the studio actually earned from her classes" available in the data.

## Lavie's Hypothetical August Salary — Flat Per-Class Headcount Tiers (No Base)

Same August dataset as before (all 35 classes with at least one commission-eligible attendee: 42 scheduled sessions, 32 with at least one paying attendee under the studio's ARRIVED-only counting vs. 35 under the "counts once booked/credit-deducted" rule I used previously — I kept the same rule here for consistency with the prior calculation).

|---|---|---|
| Group | 1 | 125,000 |
| Group | 2 | 175,000 |
| Group | 3 | 225,000 |
| Group | 4 | 275,000 |
| Private | 1 | 150,000 |
| Private | 2 | 200,000 |

**Her actual August class distribution:**
| Format / headcount | # classes | Rate | Subtotal |
|---|---|---|---|
| Group, 1 person | 17 | 125,000 | 2,125,000 |
| Group, 2 people | 11 | 175,000 | 1,925,000 |
| Group, 3 people | 2 | 225,000 | 450,000 |
| Group, 4 people | 0 | 275,000 | 0 |
| Private, 1 person | 5 | 150,000 | 750,000 |
| Private, 2 people | 0 | 200,000 | 0 |

**Total hypothetical salary: 5,250,000 VND**

No August class hit a group headcount of 4 or a private headcount of 2, so those tiers didn't come into play this month.

For reference against the two other numbers now on the table:
- Actual August pay (current `FIXED_HEADCOUNT` model): **6,250,000 VND**
- 18% revenue + 4,000,000 base (last calculation): **8,234,950 VND**
- This flat per-headcount structure: **5,250,000 VND** — about **1,000,000 VND (-16%) lower** than what she actually earned in August.

content: Okay. So we have recently sold a duo private class package. Now the problem with this is that we have a few different class types in this system. We have a group class and a private class and a matt class type. We don't publicly advertise packages for Duo private. However, when people are booking a class online, they have an option to make their private class a Duo private class, which ends up costing one point three million Vietnamese Dong rather than eight hundred and fifty thousand for just a single person private class. Selling a duo private class package is obviously a very rare occurrence since we've been open for about a year now, and this is the first time that we have sold one. However, we need to figure out how to support this in the system, and so people can actually use their duo private class packages when booking a class. So how should we add support for this package? and also be able to display it on the client's profile when they log in and be able to book their duo private class and use their package credits. As the dual private class package credits are applied to the private class type. Before writing any code at all, I would like you to have a full understanding of how the Soul Pilates CRM system works, how the package credits work, different package types, different class types, customer profiles, booking, checkout POS, calendar, everything.

content.content:
1	# Soul Pilates CRM — Full System Documentation
2	
3	> Generated by a systematic pass over the codebase. Covers architecture, data model,
4	> every backend service and controller, background jobs, integrations, and the
5	> frontend. Sizes at time of writing: **44 controllers, 65 services, 72 entities,
6	> 51 interfaces, 59 Astro pages, ~43k lines of C#.**
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 1. What this system is
11	
12	Soul Pilates CRM is the end-to-end management platform for a Pilates studio in
13	Da Nang, Vietnam. It runs three distinct surfaces off one backend + database:
14	
15	1. **Customer booking portal** — public class schedule, booking/reservation,
16	   guest & account checkout, package purchase, self-service cancel/reschedule,
17	   waitlist, customer accounts.
18	2. **Staff/Admin panel** — scheduling, clients, classes, POS, invoicing,
19	   bookings, expenses & P&L, payroll, KPI bonuses, analytics, settings, exports.
20	3. **Instructor portal** — an instructor's own schedule, earnings, hours (shifts),
21	   and self-service class management.
22	
23	There is also an **isolated fork** ("Studio Nexis") running on the same VPS with its
24	own stack, database, ports, and secrets.
25	
26	---
27	
28	## 2. Technology stack
29	
30	| Layer | Technology |
31	|---|---|
32	| Backend | ASP.NET Core (.NET 10), C# |
33	| Database | MongoDB 8 (driver 3.7) |
34	| Cache/queue | Redis 7 (where used), in-process Channel for push |
35	| Object storage | RustFS (S3-compatible, via AWSSDK.S3) |
36	| Frontend | Astro 6 (SSR/islands), vanilla JS in-page |
37	| Payments | Stripe (embedded Checkout / PaymentIntents), keys AES-encrypted in DB |
38	| Email | Brevo SMTP (transactional) |
39	| Push | Web Push (VAPID), Lib.Net.Http.WebPush |
40	| PDF | QuestPDF (invoices/receipts) |
41	| Excel | ClosedXML (data export) |
42	| Marketing | Meta Conversions API, TikTok Events API (dual pixel + server-side) |
43	| Observability | Serilog → console + file; Sentry SDK → self-hosted GlitchTip |
44	| Analytics | First-party visitor tracking + optional Google Analytics config |
45	
46	### Solution projects
47	- **SoulPilates.API** — controllers, `Program.cs`, middleware, hosted-service host, authorization.
48	- **SoulPilates.Core** — entities, DTOs, interfaces, configuration POCOs (no logic).
49	- **SoulPilates.Services** — all business logic (65 services + background services).
50	- **SoulPilates.Infrastructure** — `MongoDbContext` (thin Mongo access layer).
51	- **SoulPilates.Migration** — one-off data migration tooling.
52	- **SoulPilates.Tests** — test project (noted as rotted/non-compiling in a prior review).
53	
54	---
55	
56	## 3. Application startup & cross-cutting architecture (`Program.cs`)
57	
58	Boot sequence and the middleware/service wiring:
59	
60	### Logging & error tracking
61	- **Serilog** is bootstrapped *before* the host so startup failures (Mongo refused,
62	  bad JWT secret) are captured. Full config from `appsettings.json` → console + file sink.
63	- **Sentry** (`UseSentry`) points at a self-hosted GlitchTip when `SentrySettings:Dsn`
64	  is set; no-ops otherwise. PII is scrubbed via `SentryScrubber.BeforeSend`. `SendDefaultPii=false`.
65	- `UseSerilogRequestLogging` emits one structured line per request (method/path/status/ms),
66	  escalating level by status (≥500 Error, ≥400 Warning).
67	
68	### Dependency injection (lifetimes)
69	- **Singletons:** `MongoDbContext`, `IMediaStorage` (RustFS/S3), `IDocumentRenderer`
70	  (QuestPDF), `IGeoIpResolver`, the push `Channel<PushJob>`, and the module
71	  authorization policy provider.
72	- **Scoped:** essentially every business service (`IAuthService`, `ISchedulingService`,
73	  `IPaymentService`, `IAccountingService`, `IWalletService`, `ISettingsService`, …).
74	- **Registration order matters** in a few places (documented inline): `IWaitlistService`
75	  before scheduling/customer-auth; `IStaffRateRevisionService` before payroll/staff.
76	
77	### Hosted (background) services
78	Registered in `Program.cs` (detailed in §8):
79	`PackageExpiryBackgroundService`, `BookingReminderBackgroundService`,
80	`RetentionReminderBackgroundService`, `ReviewRequestBackgroundService`,
81	`BirthdayEmailBackgroundService`, `VipEmailBackgroundService`,
82	`ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService`, `ReservationCleanupBackgroundService`,
83	`UserStaffLinker`, `OwnerSeederHostedService`, `PushDispatcherService`,
84	`ClassReminderJob`, `NotificationSeederHostedService`,
85	`SessionCompletionBackgroundService`, `AdminSeederHostedService`.
86	> **Removed:** `UpdateCheckerService` — a covert remote "kill-switch" that phoned home
87	> to an external server and shut the app down on a ~60s timer whenever that server was
88	> unreachable. It is intentionally **not registered** and the startup validation call
89	> was removed.
90	
91	### Authentication & authorization
92	- **JWT bearer** auth. Tokens signed with `JwtSettings:Secret`; the validator accepts
93	  the current secret **and** an optional `JwtSettings:PreviousSecret` to support
94	  zero-downtime key rotation (old tokens keep validating until they expire).
95	- `ValidateIssuer=false`, `ValidateAudience=false`, `RequireHttpsMetadata=false`
96	  (TLS terminates at the reverse proxy).
97	- **Roles:** Admin, SuperAdmin, Owner, Manager, Receptionist, Accountant, Instructor, Customer.
98	- **Per-module authorization:** a custom `ModulePolicyProvider` + `ModuleAuthorizationHandler`
99	  implement `Module:{key}` policies. Access is granted by **role defaults**
100	  (`GlobalSettings.RoleAccessSettings`) OR a per-user `module` claim
101	  (`User.AllowedAdminModules`, "custom access mode"). This drives which admin pages
102	  each staff member can see/use.
103	
104	### Rate limiting
105	- `auth-login`: fixed-window per-IP, **10 req / 60s** (login + verify-email endpoints).
106	- `auth-register`: fixed-window per-IP, **5 req / 60s** (customer register).
107	- Rejections return RFC-7807 ProblemDetails with `retryAfter`, HTTP 429; client IP
108	  resolved from `RemoteIpAddress` (populated by ForwardedHeaders from the proxy).
109	
110	### Middleware pipeline (order)
111	`UnhandledExceptionMiddleware` (RFC-7807 for any crash) → Serilog request logging →
112	Swagger (dev only) → CORS → **Authentication** → RateLimiter → `CorrelationEnricherMiddleware`
113	(pushes authenticated UserId onto the log context) → **Authorization** → controllers.
114	
115	### Configuration & secrets
116	- Mongo, storage, admin-seed, web-push, Sentry, JWT all bound from configuration
117	  (env vars in prod via `__` mapping, e.g. `JwtSettings__Secret`).
118	- **Stripe keys** are *not* in config — they live **AES-256 encrypted in the settings
119	  document** and are managed from Settings → Payments. `PaymentService` decrypts on demand.
120	- **CRITICAL deployment note:** the frontend must be built with
121	  `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn`; the default `localhost:5000`
122	  breaks all API calls. Prod images are prebuilt on the VPS (`docker build` then
123	  `docker compose ... up -d backend frontend`); `docker compose build` is a no-op.

127	## 4. Data access (`MongoDbContext`)
128	
129	A thin singleton wrapper over `IMongoDatabase`:
130	- Constructed from `MongoDbSettings` (connection string + database name).
131	- Exposes `Database` (raw `IMongoDatabase`, used by the export/backup feature) and a
132	  generic `GetCollection<T>(name)` used by every service.
133	- **Convention:** entity IDs are C# `string` with `[BsonRepresentation(ObjectId)]`,
134	  stored as real ObjectIds. Cross-document references (e.g. `Attendance.CalendarSessionId`)
135	  are stored as **ObjectId**, so raw mongosh queries must wrap ids in `ObjectId(...)`.
136	- The app reads settings from the **`Settings`** collection (a stray `GlobalSettings`
137	  collection also exists but is not the source of truth).
138	- Container timezone is `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` (UTC+7); stored datetimes are UTC and must be
139	  converted for display (see `StudioTime` helper).

344	- **PushController** `push` — VAPID key, subscribe/unsubscribe, devices, test, preferences.
345	- **NotificationRuleController** `notification-rules` `[Admin]` — the (category × role) matrix.
346	- **EmailLogController** `email-logs` `[Admin,Owner,SuperAdmin]` — list + detail (with HTML body).
347	- **ExportController** `export` `[Admin]` — `business` (xlsx/csv/json) + `backup` (json/zip).
348	- **AuditLogController** `admin/audit-log` `[Admin,Manager]` — list + per-entity timeline.
349	- **MediaController** `media` `[Admin]` — class/equipment/instructor image upload + delete.
350	- **StudioRentalsController** `studio-rentals` — rental dashboard/instructors/classes/finalize.
351	- **RemindersController** `admin/reminders` `[Admin,Owner]` — manual `run` of due reminders.
352	- **CustomerMigrationController** `customer-migration` `[Admin,SuperAdmin,Owner]` — send account-activation invites.
353	- **DevSeedController** `dev` — demo seed/purge (dev only).
354	
355	---
356	
357	## 8. Background / hosted services (the "cron")
358	
359	All run in-process as `BackgroundService`/`IHostedService`. Cadences:
360	
361	| Service | Cadence | What it does |
362	|---|---|---|
363	| **ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService** | every 6h | Materialises `CalendarSession` rows from blueprint `WeeklySlots` on a rolling horizon (default 30 days). |
364	| **ReservationCleanupBackgroundService** | admin-configurable (~2 min) | Releases abandoned `RESERVED` holds past the expiry window, freeing capacity. |
365	| **SessionCompletionBackgroundService** | periodic | Transitions past-due `SCHEDULED` sessions → `COMPLETED` (≥1 attendee) or cancelled/empty. |
366	| **BookingReminderBackgroundService** | hourly | Drives `ReminderService` → customer class reminder emails at **24h and 1h** before class (idempotent per booking via `RemindersSent`). |
367	| **ClassReminderJob** | every 5 min | Instructor push reminder ~13–15 min before class (`InstructorReminderSent` flag). |
368	| **RetentionReminderBackgroundService** | configurable (hrs) | Drives retention check-in reminders (client inactive N days but package still has credits). |
369	| **ReviewRequestBackgroundService** | hourly | Google-review request ~2h after a client's **first** class. |
370	| **BirthdayEmailBackgroundService** | few×/day | Birthday greetings (once per client per year). |
371	| **VipEmailBackgroundService** | few×/day | One-time VIP / Super-VIP congratulations when a client crosses the threshold. |
372	| **PackageExpiryBackgroundService** | periodic | Expires packages past their expiry date. |
373	| **PushDispatcherService** | continuous | Drains the push `Channel<PushJob>` and delivers Web Push; prunes dead subs. |
374	| **AdminSeederHostedService** | once at boot | Ensures the configured admin account exists (no-op if present). |
375	| **OwnerSeederHostedService / NotificationSeederHostedService / UserStaffLinker** | once at boot | Seed owner defaults / notification-rule matrix; link User↔Staff rows. |
376	
377	> The removed **UpdateCheckerService** would have belonged here — it self-terminated the app on a timer when an external endpoint was unreachable. It is not registered.
378	
379	---
380	
381	## 9. Frontend (Astro)
382	
383	Three layouts, each with its own auth guard and navigation:
384	- **CustomerLayout** — public/customer portal. Includes Meta + TikTok pixels and the first-touch marketing-source capture (reads ttclid/fbclid/gclid/utm_source/referrer → localStorage) used for booking attribution.
385	- **AdminLayout** — staff/admin panel. Guard allows `instructor/admin/superadmin/manager/receptionist`; sidebar items are role- + module-gated (`data-roles` + `data-module`, filtered against `/api/management-access`). Hosts the "My portal" links (My hours/schedule/earnings) for linked staff, plus a client quick-search and the profile/push offcanvas.
386	- **InstructorLayout** — instructor portal. Guard allows `instructor/admin/superadmin/manager/receptionist`; includes the admin "View as" impersonation dropdown (stores `viewAsStaffId`, appends `?viewAs=` to API calls).
387	
388	### Pages by surface
389	**Public / customer:** `index`, `booking`, `booking-policy`, `checkout`, `packages` + `packages/checkout`, `account`, `my-bookings`, `my-package`, `login`, `register`, `verify-email`, `forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `onboarding` + `onboarding/package`, `instructors/` (list + profile), `404`.
390	
391	**Admin panel (`/admin/*`):** `index` (dashboard), `calendar`, `classes`, `class-blueprints` (+form), `clients` (+`client-form`, `client-profile`), `pos`, `invoices`, `bookings`, `products` (+form), `merchandise`/`stock-receipts`, `expenses`, `pnl`, `washout`, `loans`, `owners`, `partners` (+form), `promotions`, `voucher-batches`, `staff` (+`staff-form`), `staff-schedule`, `kpi-bonus`, `analytics`, `studio-rentals`, `settings`, `access`, `audit-log`, `email-log`, `export`, `login`, `change-password`.
392	
393	**Instructor portal (`/instructor/*`):** `index`, `schedule`, `earnings`, `hours` (shift calendar with week/month view).
394	
395	### Frontend conventions
396	- API base is baked at build time via `PUBLIC_API_URL` (must be the prod domain — see §3).
397	- Pages are largely server-rendered shells with vanilla in-page `<script>` calling the API with the bearer token from `localStorage`.
398	- `scripts/`: `push-client.js` (Web-Push subscribe), `register-sw.js` (PWA service worker), `update-monitor.js`.
399	- `lib/MuscleMapJS`: an interactive muscle-map used on class blueprints.
400	- **Astro gotcha:** `<style>` is scoped by default; any element created dynamically in a `<script>` won't get scoped styles — such pages use `<style is:global>` (e.g. staff-schedule, kpi-bonus, email-log).
401	
402	---
403	
404	## 10. External integrations
405	
406	- **Stripe** — embedded Checkout / PaymentIntents for deposits, full payments, and package purchases. Keys stored AES-encrypted in settings; webhook idempotency via `StripeProcessedEvent`. VND is zero-decimal. `StripeRoutingMode` supports company-account or owner-routed payouts.
407	- **Brevo SMTP** — all transactional email. Test-mode redirect/suppress guard. Now audited to `EmailLog`.
408	- **Web Push (VAPID)** — instructor/admin push notifications via an in-process queue + dispatcher; per-user prefs + (category×role) matrix.
409	- **Meta Conversions API + TikTok Events API** — server-side conversion tracking, deduplicated with the browser pixels by event id; hashed email/phone; config via env sections; funnel events (view/booking/purchase).
410	- **RustFS (S3)** — image storage with an EXIF-strip/resize/WebP pipeline.
411	- **GlitchTip (Sentry-compatible)** — error tracking; PII scrubbed.
412	- **ip-api.com** — GeoIP country resolution for visitor analytics.
413	- **Google Analytics** — optional, config-driven measurement id + event tracking toggle.
414	
415	---
416	
417	## 11. Key end-to-end workflows
418	
419	### Booking (customer)
420	1. Browse `/booking` → public schedule (`GET /api/booking/schedule`, full/private/past hidden).
421	2. `POST /api/booking/reserve` → creates a **RESERVED** attendance and holds a seat (`CurrentBookings++`). Guests matching an existing account are prompted to log in.
422	3. Checkout shows the payment methods from `checkout-settings` (currently **pay-at-studio only** — online card was disabled). Pay-at-studio / package-credit settle immediately → **BOOKED**; card would go RESERVED→intent→webhook→BOOKED.
423	4. Abandoned reservations are swept by `ReservationCleanupBackgroundService` (releases the seat).
424	5. Confirmation email (+ guest variant encouraging account creation). 24h & 1h reminders follow.
425	
426	### Class lifecycle
427	Blueprint → materialised into `CalendarSession`s (6-hourly job) → bookings accrue `CurrentBookings` → session auto-completes after end time (with ≥1 attendee) → feeds revenue/commission/KPI.
428	
429	### Money (month-end washout)
430	Revenue (invoices/payments) − fixed expenses − payroll − capital depreciation = net → split into Marketing/Savings/Owners by the configured % (or a month override) → owner distributions (equity share, then payroll/loan/reimbursement/bonus passes) + staff payables → lockable. Staff-paid expenses become reimbursements owed to the payee **after being settled** (Bonuses & Reimb. → Settle) **and** the washout recomputed.
431	
432	### Receptionist KPI (per month, auto-carried)
433	Bonus pool × unlocked % (revenue/package/review tiers + daily-task completion). Attendance commission is **shift-based** (only receptionists on shift when a class runs earn its per-head, split among them). Config lives per-month and carries forward.
434	
435	### Payroll (instructor)
436	Rates resolved from the effective-dated `StaffRateRevision` ledger → group/private class counts × flat/tiered/per-head rates (+ headcount tiers, revenue-commission tiers, base salary).
437	
438	---
439	
440	## 12. Operational notes & known issues
441	
442	- **Deploy:** build images on the VPS (`docker build` backend + frontend **with `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn`**), then `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend`. `docker compose build` is a no-op (prebuilt images).
443	- **Timezone:** everything stored UTC; the container runs UTC+7. Human-readable times must pass through `StudioTime.Local()` — historically several emails/pushes/notifications printed raw UTC (fixed).
444	- **Settings save safety:** `SettingsService.UpdateAsync` merge-preserves omitted sections; a fragile "all-defaults" heuristic once let general saves silently reset KPI + upsell config (fixed — KPI now always preserved and edited via its own endpoint; upsell dropdowns fixed to restore before save).
445	- **Capacity integrity:** `CurrentBookings` is the availability counter. Deleting attendance rows outside the app (raw DB) without decrementing it causes classes to falsely show full/empty — always use the app's remove action. A nightly reconciler would be a good hardening.
446	- **Tests:** `SoulPilates.Tests` was flagged as rotted/non-compiling in a prior review — CI-level coverage is unreliable.
447	- **Dead code:** `UpdateCheckerService.cs` (removed kill-switch) still exists on disk but is unregistered.
448	- **Studio Nexis** is a separate, isolated fork on the same VPS — do not cross-contaminate stacks/DBs/secrets.
449	
450	---
451	
452	*End of document. This reflects a systematic module-by-module pass; individual method-level
453	edge cases live in the code's (extensive) XML-doc comments.*
454
