# Soul Pilates CRM — Full System Documentation

> Generated by a systematic pass over the codebase. Covers architecture, data model,
> every backend service and controller, background jobs, integrations, and the
> frontend. Sizes at time of writing: **44 controllers, 65 services, 72 entities,
> 51 interfaces, 59 Astro pages, ~43k lines of C#.**

---

## 1. What this system is

Soul Pilates CRM is the end-to-end management platform for a Pilates studio in
Da Nang, Vietnam. It runs three distinct surfaces off one backend + database:

1. **Customer booking portal** — public class schedule, booking/reservation,
   guest & account checkout, package purchase, self-service cancel/reschedule,
   waitlist, customer accounts.
2. **Staff/Admin panel** — scheduling, clients, classes, POS, invoicing,
   bookings, expenses & P&L, payroll, KPI bonuses, analytics, settings, exports.
3. **Instructor portal** — an instructor's own schedule, earnings, hours (shifts),
   and self-service class management.

There is also an **isolated fork** ("Studio Nexis") running on the same VPS with its
own stack, database, ports, and secrets.

---

## 2. Technology stack

| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Backend | ASP.NET Core (.NET 10), C# |
| Database | MongoDB 8 (driver 3.7) |
| Cache/queue | Redis 7 (where used), in-process Channel for push |
| Object storage | RustFS (S3-compatible, via AWSSDK.S3) |
| Frontend | Astro 6 (SSR/islands), vanilla JS in-page |
| Payments | Stripe (embedded Checkout / PaymentIntents), keys AES-encrypted in DB |
| Email | Brevo SMTP (transactional) |
| Push | Web Push (VAPID), Lib.Net.Http.WebPush |
| PDF | QuestPDF (invoices/receipts) |
| Excel | ClosedXML (data export) |
| Marketing | Meta Conversions API, TikTok Events API (dual pixel + server-side) |
| Observability | Serilog → console + file; Sentry SDK → self-hosted GlitchTip |
| Analytics | First-party visitor tracking + optional Google Analytics config |

### Solution projects
- **SoulPilates.API** — controllers, `Program.cs`, middleware, hosted-service host, authorization.
- **SoulPilates.Core** — entities, DTOs, interfaces, configuration POCOs (no logic).
- **SoulPilates.Services** — all business logic (65 services + background services).
- **SoulPilates.Infrastructure** — `MongoDbContext` (thin Mongo access layer).
- **SoulPilates.Migration** — one-off data migration tooling.
- **SoulPilates.Tests** — test project (noted as rotted/non-compiling in a prior review).

---

## 3. Application startup & cross-cutting architecture (`Program.cs`)

Boot sequence and the middleware/service wiring:

### Logging & error tracking
- **Serilog** is bootstrapped *before* the host so startup failures (Mongo refused,
  bad JWT secret) are captured. Full config from `appsettings.json` → console + file sink.
- **Sentry** (`UseSentry`) points at a self-hosted GlitchTip when `SentrySettings:Dsn`
  is set; no-ops otherwise. PII is scrubbed via `SentryScrubber.BeforeSend`. `SendDefaultPii=false`.
- `UseSerilogRequestLogging` emits one structured line per request (method/path/status/ms),
  escalating level by status (≥500 Error, ≥400 Warning).

### Dependency injection (lifetimes)
- **Singletons:** `MongoDbContext`, `IMediaStorage` (RustFS/S3), `IDocumentRenderer`
  (QuestPDF), `IGeoIpResolver`, the push `Channel<PushJob>`, and the module
  authorization policy provider.
- **Scoped:** essentially every business service (`IAuthService`, `ISchedulingService`,
  `IPaymentService`, `IAccountingService`, `IWalletService`, `ISettingsService`, …).
- **Registration order matters** in a few places (documented inline): `IWaitlistService`
  before scheduling/customer-auth; `IStaffRateRevisionService` before payroll/staff.

### Hosted (background) services
Registered in `Program.cs` (detailed in §8):
`PackageExpiryBackgroundService`, `BookingReminderBackgroundService`,
`RetentionReminderBackgroundService`, `ReviewRequestBackgroundService`,
`BirthdayEmailBackgroundService`, `VipEmailBackgroundService`,
`ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService`, `ReservationCleanupBackgroundService`,
`UserStaffLinker`, `OwnerSeederHostedService`, `PushDispatcherService`,
`ClassReminderJob`, `NotificationSeederHostedService`,
`SessionCompletionBackgroundService`, `AdminSeederHostedService`.
> **Removed:** `UpdateCheckerService` — a covert remote "kill-switch" that phoned home
> to an external server and shut the app down on a ~60s timer whenever that server was
> unreachable. It is intentionally **not registered** and the startup validation call
> was removed.

### Authentication & authorization
- **JWT bearer** auth. Tokens signed with `JwtSettings:Secret`; the validator accepts
  the current secret **and** an optional `JwtSettings:PreviousSecret` to support
  zero-downtime key rotation (old tokens keep validating until they expire).
- `ValidateIssuer=false`, `ValidateAudience=false`, `RequireHttpsMetadata=false`
  (TLS terminates at the reverse proxy).
- **Roles:** Admin, SuperAdmin, Owner, Manager, Receptionist, Accountant, Instructor, Customer.
- **Per-module authorization:** a custom `ModulePolicyProvider` + `ModuleAuthorizationHandler`
  implement `Module:{key}` policies. Access is granted by **role defaults**
  (`GlobalSettings.RoleAccessSettings`) OR a per-user `module` claim
  (`User.AllowedAdminModules`, "custom access mode"). This drives which admin pages
  each staff member can see/use.

### Rate limiting
- `auth-login`: fixed-window per-IP, **10 req / 60s** (login + verify-email endpoints).
- `auth-register`: fixed-window per-IP, **5 req / 60s** (customer register).
- Rejections return RFC-7807 ProblemDetails with `retryAfter`, HTTP 429; client IP
  resolved from `RemoteIpAddress` (populated by ForwardedHeaders from the proxy).

### Middleware pipeline (order)
`UnhandledExceptionMiddleware` (RFC-7807 for any crash) → Serilog request logging →
Swagger (dev only) → CORS → **Authentication** → RateLimiter → `CorrelationEnricherMiddleware`
(pushes authenticated UserId onto the log context) → **Authorization** → controllers.

### Configuration & secrets
- Mongo, storage, admin-seed, web-push, Sentry, JWT all bound from configuration
  (env vars in prod via `__` mapping, e.g. `JwtSettings__Secret`).
- **Stripe keys** are *not* in config — they live **AES-256 encrypted in the settings
  document** and are managed from Settings → Payments. `PaymentService` decrypts on demand.
- **CRITICAL deployment note:** the frontend must be built with
  `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn`; the default `localhost:5000`
  breaks all API calls. Prod images are prebuilt on the VPS (`docker build` then
  `docker compose ... up -d backend frontend`); `docker compose build` is a no-op.

---

## 4. Data access (`MongoDbContext`)

A thin singleton wrapper over `IMongoDatabase`:
- Constructed from `MongoDbSettings` (connection string + database name).
- Exposes `Database` (raw `IMongoDatabase`, used by the export/backup feature) and a
  generic `GetCollection<T>(name)` used by every service.
- **Convention:** entity IDs are C# `string` with `[BsonRepresentation(ObjectId)]`,
  stored as real ObjectIds. Cross-document references (e.g. `Attendance.CalendarSessionId`)
  are stored as **ObjectId**, so raw mongosh queries must wrap ids in `ObjectId(...)`.
- The app reads settings from the **`Settings`** collection (a stray `GlobalSettings`
  collection also exists but is not the source of truth).
- Container timezone is `Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh` (UTC+7); stored datetimes are UTC and must be
  converted for display (see `StudioTime` helper).


---

## 5. Data model (collections & entities)

All entities extend `BaseEntity` (`Id`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`). Grouped by domain.

### 5.1 Scheduling & booking
- **ClassBlueprint** — the *template* for a class: name, format (GROUP/PRIVATE/MAT), focus area, difficulty, duration, default capacity, drop-in price, tax rate, default instructor, equipment, tags, hero image, and `WeeklySlots` (recurring day/time rules with per-slot capacity/instructor overrides). Bounds via `ValidFrom/ValidTo/ExceptionDates`. `IsFreelance` marks studio-rental blueprints.
- **WeeklySlot** — one recurring slot on a blueprint: `DayOfWeek`, `TimeOfDay`, optional capacity/instructor override.
- **CalendarSession** — a concrete dated class instance (materialised from a blueprint or created manually). Holds `StartTime/EndTime`, `Capacity`, `CurrentBookings` (the live seat counter that governs availability), `Status` (SCHEDULED/COMPLETED/CANCELLED), `IsPublic`, denormalised class/instructor fields, block info (`BlockedReason/BlockScope`), `InstructorReminderSent`, and freelance/studio-rental fields (`IsFreelance`, `FreelanceStaffId`, `FreelancePackageId`, `FreelanceHeadcount`, `FreelanceBillingMode`, `FreelanceChargeAmount`), plus `DropInPrice`.
- **Attendance** — one booking of a client on a session (the core booking record). `Status` (RESERVED/BOOKED/CHECKED_IN(ARRIVED)/CANCELLED/LATE_CANCEL/NO_SHOW), `PaymentMethod` (PAY_AT_STUDIO/PACKAGE_CREDIT/STRIPE_DEPOSIT/STRIPE_FULL), `AmountPaid`/`AmountDueAtStudio`, `Quantity` (multi-seat), `PackageInstanceId` (credit used), `BookingReference` (SP-YYMMDD-####), denormalised client contact, `BookingSource`/`MarketingSource`/`MarketingDetail` (attribution), `RemindersSent` (idempotency tags "24h"/"1h"), reschedule links, and imported commission/revenue for migrated rows.
- **WaitlistEntry** — a client waiting on a full session; auto-promoted to an Attendance when a seat frees (`PromotedAttendanceId`).
- **CompanyScheduleConfig** / **WeeklyHours** / date overrides — studio open/close hours + holidays, used by the schedule materialiser.

### 5.2 Clients & customer accounts
- **Client** — the studio-side client record (CRM). Contact info, country, medical history, tags, DOB, referral source/partner, `FirstVisitDate`, `LifetimeValue`, VIP-notified flag, retention opt-out + `UnsubscribeToken`. `IsStudioRentalProfile` marks synthetic rental clients.
- **CustomerAccount** — the customer *login* (portal). Email/password hash, `ClientId` link, email verification tokens, password-reset tokens, `StripeCustomerId`, onboarding flag, and late-reschedule usage tracking (`LateRescheduleUsedDates`, `RescheduledAttendanceIds`).
- **Tag** — named client tag with color.

### 5.3 Products, packages & wallet (credits)
- **Product** — anything sellable: class packages, merchandise, drop-ins. `Type`, price, tax, `Credits` (for packages), `ValidityDays`, `MaxFreezeDays`, freebies (`FreeSocks`, `IncludesFreePrivateClass`), POS/online visibility flags, `Variants`, stock.
- **PackageBlueprint** — package definition (credits + validity) linked to a product.
- **ClientPackage** — a *purchased* package instance (the wallet). `Format`, `TotalCredits`/`CreditsUsed`/`CreditsRemaining`, activation/expiry, `Status` (ACTIVE/LOW_BALANCE/EXPIRED/FROZEN), `FractionalValuePerClass` (for revenue attribution), and retention-reminder idempotency tags.
- **PackageFreeze** — a freeze window that extends expiry.
- **PackageLedgerLog** — append-only ledger of credit deductions/refunds per package (drives accurate refunds and audit).
- **MerchandiseSku** / **StockReceipt** / **LowStockAlert** — inventory: per-variant SKUs with stock, goods-received receipts (with cost lines), and low-stock alert dedupe.

### 5.4 Invoicing & payments
- **Invoice** — a sale. `InvoiceNumber`, client, gross/discount/tax/net totals, `Status` (PAID/UNPAID/VOID), payment method, `OnlineFeeAmount`, links to voucher/promo redemptions, `Lines`.
- **InvoiceLine** — a line item: product, qty, unit price, discount, `AttendanceId`/`CalendarSessionId` links, `ProductTypeSnapshot` (used for package-sale counting & revenue categorisation).
- **Payment** — a payment against an invoice (amount, method, date, logged-by).
- **PaymentRecord** — Stripe-side record for a booking payment: type/method, amount, currency, `Status`, Stripe intent/charge/session ids, refund info.
- **StripeProcessedEvent** — webhook idempotency (dedupes Stripe events by `EventId`).

### 5.5 Staff, rates, commission & payroll
- **Staff** — a team member: `Role`, contact, bank details, bio/photo/specialties, `UserId` link, `StudioRentalClientId`, `BaseSalary`, `EmploymentStartDate`, and a full **commission model** (`CommissionModel`, group/private flat or tiered rates, per-head rates, headcount tiers, revenue-commission tiers, free-class rates).
- **StaffRateRevision** — versioned snapshot of a staff member's rate/commission config, effective-dated (so payroll uses the rate in force at the time).
- **MonthlyCommissionOverride** — per-staff, per-month commission override.
- **CommissionTier / HeadcountPayoutTier / RevenueCommissionTier** — the tier value objects used in commission models.
- **PayrollRun** — a computed payroll period with per-instructor `Results` (rate snapshot + group/private class counts + earnings + revenue commission + total pay).

### 5.6 Owners, accounting & the monthly "washout"
- **OwnerProfile** — an owner: `StaffId`, `EquitySharePercentage`, `ReceivesStripePayouts`, `IsActiveOwner`.
- **MonthlyWashout** — the monthly money-flow computation: revenue (sales vs earned), payroll, fixed expenses, salaries, capital depreciation, net-before-allocations, the three allocations (marketing/savings/owners) with the % applied, revenue-by-category/method, net income, referral commissions, and a `Locked` flag.
- **OwnerDistribution** — per-owner, per-month payout line: owners-pool share by equity, minus Stripe deduction, plus reimbursements/commissions/bonuses, ± loan adjustment → `TotalPayable`, with paid status.
- **StaffPayable** — per-non-owner-staff, per-month payout: salary + reimbursement + commission + bonus (+ receptionist attendance commission + KPI bonus) → total, paid status.
- **OwnerLoan / OwnerLoanPayment** — inter-owner loans and their repayments (auto/manual), feeding the loan-adjustment column.
- **CapitalInvestment** — capital assets with depreciation schedule; `IsPreOpening` marks founding investment to recover (payback tracking).
- **MonthlyAllocationOverride** — per-month override of the marketing/savings/owners split percentages.
- **Bonus** — a discretionary bonus to a staff member for a month (authorised-by, paid status).
- **ReimbursementSettleBatch** — audit row for settling staff-paid expenses into a month's washout.

### 5.7 Expenses & fund pools
- **Expense** — an expense row: category, amount, `Type` (OPEX/CAPEX/COGS), `PaidBy` (COMPANY/STAFF — STAFF needs reimbursement, with the full settlement fields), `PaidStatus`/`OutstandingAmount`, `FundSource` (OPERATIONS/MARKETING/SAVINGS — the reserve pools are drawn down instead of counting in month fixed expenses), `SalaryForStaffId` (salary lines), vendor, receipt.
- Fund pools (Marketing / Savings reserves) are derived from allocations + `FundSource` expenses (see `FundPoolService`).

### 5.8 Receptionist KPI & daily tasks
- **ReceptionistKpiMonthOverride** — the full **per-month** KPI config (bonus pool, tiers for revenue/packages/reviews, daily tasks, per-head attendance commission, completion %, split mode) + live inputs (Google review count, notes). Auto-carried-forward from the prior month.
- **ReceptionistKpiTier** — a tier (label, goal, reward %).
- **ReceptionistDailyTaskDefinition** — a recurring daily task.
- **ReceptionistDailyCustomTask** — a one-off task for a specific date (counts toward the day's completion).
- **ReceptionistDailyTaskLog** — per-receptionist, per-day record of completed task ids.

### 5.9 Partners, referrals, vouchers & promotions
- **Partner** — a referral partner (business): referral code, discount %, commission tiers, eligible product types, status.
- **PartnerCommissionTier** — partner commission by package quantity.
- **PartnerPayable / RefereePayout** — monthly partner commission owed, with per-invoice line breakdown.
- **VoucherBatch / VoucherRedemption** — physical voucher drops by partners and their redemptions.
- **Promotion / PromoRedemption** — promo codes (type/value, validity, redemption caps per code and per client, min subtotal, eligible types) and their use.

### 5.10 Marketing & web analytics
- **VisitorEvent** — first-party analytics event (page view / funnel step): visitor/session ids, path, referrer + resolved source, country (GeoIP), new-visitor flag, funnel step.

### 5.11 Notifications, push & email
- **User** — the staff/admin login: role, `StaffId` link, `NotificationPreferences`, `MustChangePassword`, `AllowedAdminModules` + `UseCustomModuleAccess` (custom access mode).
- **NotificationRule** — per (category × role) toggle for push, with email fallback and lock flags.
- **NotificationPreferences** — per-user push prefs with per-category overrides.
- **PushSubscription** — a browser Web-Push subscription (endpoint, keys, failure count).
- **EmailTemplate / EmailTemplateDefaults** — customisable transactional email templates (subject/body, variables, enabled flag, defaults).
- **EmailLog** — audit of every outbound email (to, subject, status SENT/FAILED/SUPPRESSED/REDIRECTED, error, redirect target, and the rendered HTML body).

### 5.12 Settings, access & audit
- **GlobalSettings** — the single settings document (collection `Settings`). Holds: P&L allocation split (marketing/savings/owners must sum to 100), cancellation windows (per format × payment tier), late-reschedule policy, expense categories, Stripe routing mode + **encrypted Stripe keys** + enabled flag, online-fee %, studio-rental pricing, the full receptionist-KPI defaults (now seed-only), role-access matrix, checkout options (online/partial/full/pay-at-studio, deposit %, guest checkout), package-upsell config, retention-reminder config, waitlist/reservation/email-verification toggles, VIP thresholds, Google Analytics config, company schedule, materialisation horizon, and email templates.
- **RoleAccessSetting / RoleModuleDefinition** — the admin-module access matrix and module catalog.
- **DashboardLayout** — per-user admin dashboard widget layout.
- **AuditLog** — actor/action/entity before-after diffs with correlation id + IP.
- **MigrationImportLog** — idempotency for the spreadsheet importers.

---

## 6. Services (business logic)

65 services in `SoulPilates.Services`. Grouped by domain; background/hosted services are in §8.

### 6.1 Scheduling & booking
- **SchedulingService** — the heart of scheduling. Blueprint CRUD, session materialisation, manual/freelance sessions, booking (`BookClientAsync`), reservation flow (reserve → RESERVED holds capacity → pay → BOOKED), `CleanupExpiredReservationsAsync`, `CheckInClientAsync`, `CollectStudioPaymentAsync` (POS/credit/pay-at-studio settle), admin add-student, `AdminRescheduleBookingAsync`, block/unblock/override slots, `CompleteFreelanceSessionAsync`, capacity reserve/release helpers (`ReserveSessionCapacity`/`ReleaseSessionCapacity`, atomic `$inc` guarded so it can't exceed capacity or go negative), booking-source breakdown, and roster/day queries. Owns `CurrentBookings` integrity.
- **WaitlistService** — FIFO waitlist for full sessions; `JoinAsync`, `TryPromoteNextAsync` (called on a cancel), position/active queries. Registered before scheduling because both scheduling and customer-auth depend on it.
- **StaffShiftService** — staff work shifts: recurring (weekly, multi-day `DaysOfWeek`) or one-off, with lunch `Breaks`, validity bounds, and per-date exceptions. `GetScheduleAsync` expands definitions into concrete dated occurrences (used by the schedule UI and by receptionist attendance-commission shift matching).
- **InstructorService** — instructor self-service reads: redacted profile, upcoming schedule, current-month earnings, and class-days (fixed to use UTC-specified month windows to avoid the container-TZ off-by-one).
- **StudioRentalService** — studio-rental (freelance) dashboard, instructors, and classes.

### 6.2 Clients, customer accounts & auth
- **AuthService** — staff/admin login (`AuthenticateAsync`) + `ChangePasswordAsync`. Issues JWTs (7-day) with role, `staff_id` (when linked), and per-module claims. Accepts current + previous JWT secret.
- **CustomerAuthService** — the customer portal: register (with email/phone dup checks + `MatchExistingAccountAsync`), login, email verification, my-bookings/packages, self-service cancel (`CancelBookingAsync` → triggers waitlist promotion), reschedule (`RescheduleBookingAsync` with eligibility + late-reschedule grace), onboarding, forgot/reset password. Emits push notifications on cancel/reschedule.
- **ClientService** — CRM client CRUD, search, phone/email lookup, last-visit + checked-in counts (used for VIP tiering).
- **PasswordHasher** — BCrypt hash/verify (work factor 12), shared by staff + customer accounts.

### 6.3 Payments, invoicing & products
- **PaymentService** — Stripe deposits/full payments ("guarantee your spot" deposit model). Reads Stripe keys from the encrypted settings at runtime. `QuotePriceAsync`, `CreateIntentAsync`, `MarkSucceededAsync` (RESERVED→BOOKED + AmountPaid), `HandleWebhookAsync` (idempotent via `StripeProcessedEvent`), package-purchase intents, `FinalizeCheckoutSessionAsync`. VND is zero-decimal (no ×100).
- **InvoiceService** — invoice create (with lines, discounts, tax, referral commission), add payment, void, refund, receipt PDF render, list/detail queries.
- **ProductService** — product CRUD (packages, merch, drop-ins).
- **MerchandiseSkuService** — per-variant inventory CRUD + atomic filter-guarded stock `$inc` (`TryDeductAsync`), mirrors voucher redemption's atomicity.
- **StockReceiptService** — goods-received receipts that increment SKU stock.
- **WalletService** — the package-credit engine: grant, `DeductCreditAsync` (atomic, all-or-nothing per request), refund (ledger-driven via `PackageLedgerLog`, with legacy fallback), forfeit-on-late-cancel, freeze, adjust, `ExpireOldPackagesAsync`, active-package resolution by client + format.

### 6.4 Accounting, payroll, owners & funds
- **AccountingService** — the month-end **washout** pipeline: aggregate revenue (per category + method) from invoices/payments, fixed expenses + payroll + capital depreciation, compute net, apply the three allocations (marketing/savings/owners), build owner distributions (equity → payroll → loan → reimbursement → bonus passes) + staff payables, referral commissions, P&L grid, payback summary, reimbursement settle workflow (`SettleReimbursementsAsync` folds STAFF-paid expenses into a month's payables), bonuses, lock month.
- **PayrollService** — instructor payroll computed from `Staff` rates resolved via the immutable `StaffRateRevision` ledger as-of the period end. Handles group/private, flat vs tiered, per-head + headcount tiers (marginal or flat), revenue-commission tiers, base salary.
- **StaffRateRevisionService** — versioned, effective-dated staff rate ledger; `ResolveAsOfAsync` returns the rate in force at a date; diff detection to avoid noise.
- **OwnerService** — owner (Staff + OwnerProfile) CRUD + default seeding.
- **OwnerLoanService** — inter-owner loans + repayments (validated: distinct parties, both owners), feeding loan adjustments in the washout.
- **FundPoolService** — derives Marketing/Savings reserve balances from washout allocations (credits) minus `FundSource` expenses (debits) — no separate balance doc to drift; exposes pool ledger.
- **ReceptionistKpiService** — the per-month receptionist KPI engine (bonus pool + tiers for revenue/packages/reviews + daily-task completion + **shift-based** attendance commission). Auto-carries config forward per month; custom daily tasks; folds results into `StaffPayable` via `ApplyReceptionistCompToPayablesAsync`.

### 6.5 Analytics & tracking
- **AnalyticsService** — read-only aggregations for dashboards: dashboard KPIs, top clients, top class times, customer segmentation, country distribution, attendance rates, occupancy, booking lead time, cohort retention, month/business summary, daily time series, revenue breakdown, instructor performance, booking-source + payment-method distribution, yearly revenue/expense. (These are the natural "tools" for a data chatbot.)
- **VisitorAnalyticsService** — first-party web analytics: `TrackAsync` (from the public beacon), live visitor count, visitor summary, booking funnel, signup sources.
- **GeoIpResolver** — IP→country via ip-api.com with an in-process cache.
- **MetaConversionsService / TiktokEventsService** — server-side conversion event senders (Meta CAPI / TikTok Events API), config via env sections; deduplicated with the browser pixels by event id.

### 6.6 Communications (email, push, notifications)
- **EmailService** — all transactional email via Brevo SMTP: booking/guest confirmation, class reminder, cancellation, receipt, activation/verification, password reset, birthday, VIP/Super-VIP, review request, generic. Test-mode safety net (suppress/redirect). Times converted to studio-local. Now logs every send to `EmailLog` (with body).
- **EmailLogService** — stores + serves the outbound-email audit log (best-effort).
- **PushService** — Web-Push subscription management + enqueues payloads onto the in-process channel (fire-and-forget).
- **PushDispatcherService** (hosted) — drains the channel and delivers via Web Push; prunes dead subscriptions on 410/404.
- **NotificationPublisher** — "push-first, email-fallback" policy engine; `PublishAsync`/`PublishToRolesAsync` respect per-user prefs + the notification-rule matrix.
- **NotificationRuleService** — the (category × role) notification matrix with unique index + default seeding.
- **ReminderService / RetentionReminderService / ReviewRequestService / BirthdayEmailService / VipEmailService** — the "due-window" senders driven by their hosted timers (see §8).

### 6.7 Referrals, vouchers, promotions
- **PartnerService** — referral partner CRUD.
- **RefereeCommissionCalculator** — pure functions computing partner commission on invoice lines by tier.
- **VoucherService** — voucher batches + atomic redemption (`RedeemAsync`).
- **PromotionService** — customer promo-code lifecycle: preview (generic rejection to avoid probing), redeem (caps per code + per client), CRUD.

### 6.8 Platform, media, settings, audit
- **SettingsService** — the singleton settings document. Merge-preserving `UpdateAsync` that carries forward sections a partial save omits (VIP, Stripe keys, KPI config now always preserved, email templates, schedule, reservation, upsell) — the safeguard that prevents unrelated saves from wiping config; allocation-split validation (must sum to 100); email-template + schedule + horizon management; decrypted Stripe config accessor.
- **SettingsEncryptionHelper** — AES-256-CBC at-rest encryption for Stripe secrets; key derived (PBKDF2/SHA-256, 100k iterations) from the JWT secret.
- **MediaStorageService** — S3/RustFS image pipeline: decode → strip EXIF → resize → WebP q80 → PUT with immutable cache headers.
- **QuestPdfDocumentRenderer** — PDF rendering (invoices/receipts).
- **ExportService** — the data export/backup feature (business datasets → Excel/CSV/JSON via ClosedXML + zip; full raw JSON backup of every collection; secrets redacted).
- **AuditLogger / AuditLogService** — write-side (captures actor/IP/correlation from HttpContext, falls back to "system") and read-side (timeline + list) of the audit log.
- **StudioTime** — the studio timezone helper (UTC→UTC+7) that every human-readable time must pass through.
- **PhoneSplitter** — splits concatenated phone numbers into dial-code + national number.
- **UpdateCheckerService** — **dead code**: the removed covert kill-switch. File still exists but is not registered anywhere.

---

## 7. API surface (controllers)

44 controllers. Auth shown as `[roles]`; endpoints are relative to the route. Anonymous
customer-facing routes are marked. All under `/api`.

### 7.1 Public / customer portal
- **BookingController** `booking` `[Customer + AllowAnonymous mix]` — the public booking API: `schedule` (public class list, hides full/private-restricted + past), `class/{id}`, `instructors`, `equipment`, `identify` (guest lookup by phone/email), **`reserve`** (creates RESERVED hold; guest guard prompts login if an account matches), `release-reservation`, `client-context`, `confirmation/{ref}`, waitlist join/me/leave/session-list.
- **CustomerAuthController** `customer` `[Customer]` — register, login, verify-email, me, my-bookings, cancel-booking, cancel-policy, reschedule-booking + eligibility, reset-reschedule-grace, my-packages, profile, onboarding, forgot/reset-password. (login/register/verify are rate-limited.)
- **PackagePurchaseController** `package-purchase` `[Customer]` — featured packages, Stripe checkout, confirm.
- **PaymentController** `payment` — `quote`, `checkout-settings` (public: which payment methods to show), `create-intent`, `confirm`, `confirm-session`, **`webhook`** (Stripe).
- **RetentionController** `retention` — `unsubscribe` (one-click email unsubscribe token).
- **MetaTrackingController** `meta` / **TiktokTrackingController** `tiktok` — `config` + `event` (browser pixel config + server-side event relay).

### 7.2 Scheduling, classes, instructors
- **SchedulingController** `scheduling` `[Admin,Manager,Receptionist,Instructor]` — the admin scheduling surface: classes list, session CRUD, `book`, `check-in`, booking status/flags/remove, `collect-payment`, `reschedule`, `split`, `walk-in-checkout`, block/unblock/override, freelance sessions + complete, day view, `bookings/sources` (attribution), CSV export.
- **ClassBlueprintController** `classblueprint` — blueprint CRUD + featured toggle.
- **InstructorController** `instructor` `[Instructor,Admin,SuperAdmin,Owner]` — instructor portal: clients, me, schedule, bookings, earnings, class-days, calendar, manual session, block/reschedule/transfer sessions, add/remove student, attendee profile. Supports `?viewAs={staffId}` admin impersonation.
- **StaffShiftController** `staff-shifts` `[Admin,Manager,Receptionist]` — shift CRUD, `occurrences`, `{id}/skip`, and `mine/occurrences` (self-service, honours `viewAs` for admins).
- **EquipmentController** `equipment` — equipment CRUD (+ `public`).

### 7.3 Clients, staff, owners
- **ClientController** `client` — client list/detail/create/update + `vips`.
- **StaffController** `staff` `[Admin]` — staff CRUD, active-status, login provisioning (`{id}/login` create/link/unlink), rate revisions, commission overrides.
- **OwnerController** `owners` / **OwnerLoanController** `owner-loans** `[Admin]` — owner profile CRUD; inter-owner loans + payments.
- **UserAccessController** `user-access` `[Admin,SuperAdmin,Owner]` — per-user admin-module access (modules catalog, set/reset a user's granted modules).
- **ManagementAccessController** `management-access` — returns the caller's effective role + granted modules (drives sidebar visibility + page guards).

### 7.4 Finance & accounting
- **InvoiceController** `invoice` `[Admin,Receptionist,Accountant]` — recent/list/detail, create, add payment, receipt PDF, CSV export, void, refund.
- **AccountingController** `accounting` `[Admin,Accountant]` — expenses, monthly salaries, mark-paid, **washout** compute/summary/lock, owner distributions, reimbursements (list/summary/settle), staff-payables, bonuses CRUD + mark-paid, partner payables + payouts, P&L grid, payback summary, fund pools + ledger.
- **PayrollController** `payroll` `[Admin,Accountant]` — `run` (compute a payroll period).
- **PartnerController** `partner` / **VoucherController** `voucher-batches` / **PromotionController** `promotions` — referral partners; voucher batches + redeem; promo codes + preview/redeem.
- **WalletController** `wallet` — active packages, per-client wallet, freeze, adjust-credit, expiry, grant-package.
- **ProductController** `product` / **MerchandiseSkuController** `merchandise` / **StockReceiptController** `stock-receipts` — products; SKUs; goods-received.

### 7.5 KPI, analytics, tracking
- **ReceptionistKpiController** `receptionist-kpi` `[Admin,Receptionist]` — dashboard, month-config, month-settings (full per-month config), custom-tasks CRUD, daily-tasks log.
- **AnalyticsController** `analytics` `[Admin,Accountant]` — the ~18 analytics reads + `ga-config`.
- **TrackingController** `track` — `POST` beacon (public write) + admin visitor reads (live/summary/funnel/signup-sources).

### 7.6 Platform, settings, comms, admin tooling
- **AuthController** `auth` — `login` + `change-password` (rate-limited).
- **MeController** `me` — self profile/name/password + dashboard layout.
- **SettingsController** `settings` `[Admin]` — get/save settings, retention/VIP PATCH, allocation overrides, schedule, materialisation horizon, email templates CRUD + enabled, **stripe-keys** (encrypted).
- **PushController** `push` — VAPID key, subscribe/unsubscribe, devices, test, preferences.
- **NotificationRuleController** `notification-rules` `[Admin]` — the (category × role) matrix.
- **EmailLogController** `email-logs` `[Admin,Owner,SuperAdmin]` — list + detail (with HTML body).
- **ExportController** `export` `[Admin]` — `business` (xlsx/csv/json) + `backup` (json/zip).
- **AuditLogController** `admin/audit-log` `[Admin,Manager]` — list + per-entity timeline.
- **MediaController** `media` `[Admin]` — class/equipment/instructor image upload + delete.
- **StudioRentalsController** `studio-rentals` — rental dashboard/instructors/classes/finalize.
- **RemindersController** `admin/reminders` `[Admin,Owner]` — manual `run` of due reminders.
- **CustomerMigrationController** `customer-migration` `[Admin,SuperAdmin,Owner]` — send account-activation invites.
- **DevSeedController** `dev` — demo seed/purge (dev only).

---

## 8. Background / hosted services (the "cron")

All run in-process as `BackgroundService`/`IHostedService`. Cadences:

| Service | Cadence | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| **ScheduleMaterialiserBackgroundService** | every 6h | Materialises `CalendarSession` rows from blueprint `WeeklySlots` on a rolling horizon (default 30 days). |
| **ReservationCleanupBackgroundService** | admin-configurable (~2 min) | Releases abandoned `RESERVED` holds past the expiry window, freeing capacity. |
| **SessionCompletionBackgroundService** | periodic | Transitions past-due `SCHEDULED` sessions → `COMPLETED` (≥1 attendee) or cancelled/empty. |
| **BookingReminderBackgroundService** | hourly | Drives `ReminderService` → customer class reminder emails at **24h and 1h** before class (idempotent per booking via `RemindersSent`). |
| **ClassReminderJob** | every 5 min | Instructor push reminder ~13–15 min before class (`InstructorReminderSent` flag). |
| **RetentionReminderBackgroundService** | configurable (hrs) | Drives retention check-in reminders (client inactive N days but package still has credits). |
| **ReviewRequestBackgroundService** | hourly | Google-review request ~2h after a client's **first** class. |
| **BirthdayEmailBackgroundService** | few×/day | Birthday greetings (once per client per year). |
| **VipEmailBackgroundService** | few×/day | One-time VIP / Super-VIP congratulations when a client crosses the threshold. |
| **PackageExpiryBackgroundService** | periodic | Expires packages past their expiry date. |
| **PushDispatcherService** | continuous | Drains the push `Channel<PushJob>` and delivers Web Push; prunes dead subs. |
| **AdminSeederHostedService** | once at boot | Ensures the configured admin account exists (no-op if present). |
| **OwnerSeederHostedService / NotificationSeederHostedService / UserStaffLinker** | once at boot | Seed owner defaults / notification-rule matrix; link User↔Staff rows. |

> The removed **UpdateCheckerService** would have belonged here — it self-terminated the app on a timer when an external endpoint was unreachable. It is not registered.

---

## 9. Frontend (Astro)

Three layouts, each with its own auth guard and navigation:
- **CustomerLayout** — public/customer portal. Includes Meta + TikTok pixels and the first-touch marketing-source capture (reads ttclid/fbclid/gclid/utm_source/referrer → localStorage) used for booking attribution.
- **AdminLayout** — staff/admin panel. Guard allows `instructor/admin/superadmin/manager/receptionist`; sidebar items are role- + module-gated (`data-roles` + `data-module`, filtered against `/api/management-access`). Hosts the "My portal" links (My hours/schedule/earnings) for linked staff, plus a client quick-search and the profile/push offcanvas.
- **InstructorLayout** — instructor portal. Guard allows `instructor/admin/superadmin/manager/receptionist`; includes the admin "View as" impersonation dropdown (stores `viewAsStaffId`, appends `?viewAs=` to API calls).

### Pages by surface
**Public / customer:** `index`, `booking`, `booking-policy`, `checkout`, `packages` + `packages/checkout`, `account`, `my-bookings`, `my-package`, `login`, `register`, `verify-email`, `forgot-password`, `reset-password`, `onboarding` + `onboarding/package`, `instructors/` (list + profile), `404`.

**Admin panel (`/admin/*`):** `index` (dashboard), `calendar`, `classes`, `class-blueprints` (+form), `clients` (+`client-form`, `client-profile`), `pos`, `invoices`, `bookings`, `products` (+form), `merchandise`/`stock-receipts`, `expenses`, `pnl`, `washout`, `loans`, `owners`, `partners` (+form), `promotions`, `voucher-batches`, `staff` (+`staff-form`), `staff-schedule`, `kpi-bonus`, `analytics`, `studio-rentals`, `settings`, `access`, `audit-log`, `email-log`, `export`, `login`, `change-password`.

**Instructor portal (`/instructor/*`):** `index`, `schedule`, `earnings`, `hours` (shift calendar with week/month view).

### Frontend conventions
- API base is baked at build time via `PUBLIC_API_URL` (must be the prod domain — see §3).
- Pages are largely server-rendered shells with vanilla in-page `<script>` calling the API with the bearer token from `localStorage`.
- `scripts/`: `push-client.js` (Web-Push subscribe), `register-sw.js` (PWA service worker), `update-monitor.js`.
- `lib/MuscleMapJS`: an interactive muscle-map used on class blueprints.
- **Astro gotcha:** `<style>` is scoped by default; any element created dynamically in a `<script>` won't get scoped styles — such pages use `<style is:global>` (e.g. staff-schedule, kpi-bonus, email-log).

---

## 10. External integrations

- **Stripe** — embedded Checkout / PaymentIntents for deposits, full payments, and package purchases. Keys stored AES-encrypted in settings; webhook idempotency via `StripeProcessedEvent`. VND is zero-decimal. `StripeRoutingMode` supports company-account or owner-routed payouts.
- **Brevo SMTP** — all transactional email. Test-mode redirect/suppress guard. Now audited to `EmailLog`.
- **Web Push (VAPID)** — instructor/admin push notifications via an in-process queue + dispatcher; per-user prefs + (category×role) matrix.
- **Meta Conversions API + TikTok Events API** — server-side conversion tracking, deduplicated with the browser pixels by event id; hashed email/phone; config via env sections; funnel events (view/booking/purchase).
- **RustFS (S3)** — image storage with an EXIF-strip/resize/WebP pipeline.
- **GlitchTip (Sentry-compatible)** — error tracking; PII scrubbed.
- **ip-api.com** — GeoIP country resolution for visitor analytics.
- **Google Analytics** — optional, config-driven measurement id + event tracking toggle.

---

## 11. Key end-to-end workflows

### Booking (customer)
1. Browse `/booking` → public schedule (`GET /api/booking/schedule`, full/private/past hidden).
2. `POST /api/booking/reserve` → creates a **RESERVED** attendance and holds a seat (`CurrentBookings++`). Guests matching an existing account are prompted to log in.
3. Checkout shows the payment methods from `checkout-settings` (currently **pay-at-studio only** — online card was disabled). Pay-at-studio / package-credit settle immediately → **BOOKED**; card would go RESERVED→intent→webhook→BOOKED.
4. Abandoned reservations are swept by `ReservationCleanupBackgroundService` (releases the seat).
5. Confirmation email (+ guest variant encouraging account creation). 24h & 1h reminders follow.

### Class lifecycle
Blueprint → materialised into `CalendarSession`s (6-hourly job) → bookings accrue `CurrentBookings` → session auto-completes after end time (with ≥1 attendee) → feeds revenue/commission/KPI.

### Money (month-end washout)
Revenue (invoices/payments) − fixed expenses − payroll − capital depreciation = net → split into Marketing/Savings/Owners by the configured % (or a month override) → owner distributions (equity share, then payroll/loan/reimbursement/bonus passes) + staff payables → lockable. Staff-paid expenses become reimbursements owed to the payee **after being settled** (Bonuses & Reimb. → Settle) **and** the washout recomputed.

### Receptionist KPI (per month, auto-carried)
Bonus pool × unlocked % (revenue/package/review tiers + daily-task completion). Attendance commission is **shift-based** (only receptionists on shift when a class runs earn its per-head, split among them). Config lives per-month and carries forward.

### Payroll (instructor)
Rates resolved from the effective-dated `StaffRateRevision` ledger → group/private class counts × flat/tiered/per-head rates (+ headcount tiers, revenue-commission tiers, base salary).

---

## 12. Operational notes & known issues

- **Deploy:** build images on the VPS (`docker build` backend + frontend **with `--build-arg PUBLIC_API_URL=https://soulpilates.com.vn`**), then `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml --env-file prod.env up -d backend frontend`. `docker compose build` is a no-op (prebuilt images).
- **Timezone:** everything stored UTC; the container runs UTC+7. Human-readable times must pass through `StudioTime.Local()` — historically several emails/pushes/notifications printed raw UTC (fixed).
- **Settings save safety:** `SettingsService.UpdateAsync` merge-preserves omitted sections; a fragile "all-defaults" heuristic once let general saves silently reset KPI + upsell config (fixed — KPI now always preserved and edited via its own endpoint; upsell dropdowns fixed to restore before save).
- **Capacity integrity:** `CurrentBookings` is the availability counter. Deleting attendance rows outside the app (raw DB) without decrementing it causes classes to falsely show full/empty — always use the app's remove action. A nightly reconciler would be a good hardening.
- **Tests:** `SoulPilates.Tests` was flagged as rotted/non-compiling in a prior review — CI-level coverage is unreliable.
- **Dead code:** `UpdateCheckerService.cs` (removed kill-switch) still exists on disk but is unregistered.
- **Studio Nexis** is a separate, isolated fork on the same VPS — do not cross-contaminate stacks/DBs/secrets.

---

*End of document. This reflects a systematic module-by-module pass; individual method-level
edge cases live in the code's (extensive) XML-doc comments.*

# Agent Context: .NET Backend Architecture (Soul Pilates)

## Responsibilities
This is the root of the .NET 10 solution mapping to the Soul Pilates business logic ecosystem. It follows a strict N-Tier (Clean Architecture) principle to decouple logic across API, Core, Services, and Infrastructure.

## Critical Boundaries
- **Core Layer**: Contains domain Entities and Interfaces. No business logic or external dependencies allowed here.
- **Infrastructure Layer**: Exclusively manages database connection logic (`MongoDbContext`).
- **Services Layer**: Binds Core Interfaces to concrete orchestrations. Most domain specific code (e.g., wallet washouts, payroll aggregations) lives here.
- **API Layer**: The presentation tier handling ASP.NET controllers, JWT Authorization headers, and dependency injection `Program.cs`.

## Future AI Agents Keep In Mind
- Never inject Infrastructure directly into the API controllers. Always pass through the Interfaces injected via `Program.cs`.
- When tracking references (e.g., Attendance to CalendarSession to ClassBlueprint), remember MongoDB is a document store. Joins are executed via multiple queries inside the Service layers rather than `.Include()` statements typical of EntityFramework.

input.prompt:
You are researching a live production codebase (read-only — do not modify anything) to build understanding for a design decision. Do NOT write any code or edit any files. This is pure research/reporting.

CONTEXT: Soul Pilates is a Pilates studio CRM (ASP.NET Core / .NET 10, C#, MongoDB, Astro frontend). The source lives on a remote server, NOT on this local machine. Access it via SSH:

The main repo is at /opt/soulpilates on that remote host. Plan on doing all reading through SSH command output — there's no local checkout.

YOU ALSO HAVE READ ACCESS TO THE LIVE PRODUCTION MONGODB (same server) to cross-check real data. Connect like this (never print the connection string itself — capture it into a shell variable server-side and use it, so raw credentials never appear in your output):

    ssh -i ~/.ssh/soulpilates_deploy root@51.79.226.200 bash -s <<'EOF'
    URI=$(docker exec soulpilates-prod-backend printenv MongoDbSettings__ConnectionString)
    DB=$(docker exec soulpilates-prod-backend printenv MongoDbSettings__DatabaseName)
    docker exec -e URI="$URI" -e DBN="$DB" soulpilates-prod-mongo mongosh --quiet --eval '
      var conn = new Mongo(process.env.URI);
      var db = conn.getDB(process.env.DBN);
      // your query here, e.g.:
      printjson(db.Products.find({}).limit(5).toArray());
    '
    EOF

Collections you may want: Products, ClientPackages, Invoices, InvoiceLines, PackageLedgerLogs. This is READ-ONLY — only ever run find/aggregate, never insert/update/delete.

YOUR FOCUS: how a package gets sold (POS and online) and turned into a redeemable `ClientPackage`, and specifically how the studio's one existing "Duo Private" sale was recorded. I need exact, file:line-cited answers to:

1. **ProductService / ProductController** (SoulPilates.Services, SoulPilates.API) — read the Product entity and service. What are the exact `Type` enum values for a Product (e.g. PACKAGE, MERCHANDISE, DROP_IN...)? How does creating a Product of package type relate to `PackageBlueprint`— are they the same document, or does creating a package Product auto-create/require a PackageBlueprint? Is there a `Format` field on Product that ties a package to GROUP/PRIVATE/MAT?

2. **The actual purchase flow that creates a `ClientPackage`** — trace it from a purchase (either `PackagePurchaseController`/Stripe flow, or POS/`InvoiceService` walk-in sale) through to the code that inserts a new `ClientPackage` document. Quote the exact construction of that document — where do `Format`, `TotalCredits`, `FractionalValuePerClass` get set, and from what source (the Product? the PackageBlueprint? hardcoded?).

3. **POS flow specifically** (admin `/admin/pos` — find the backend endpoints it calls, likely on InvoiceController or a POS-specific controller/service) — when staff manually sell a custom item or an ad-hoc-priced package to a walk-in client, what's the mechanism? Is there a way to sell something NOT backed by an existing `Product` (e.g., a custom line item), and if so, does that path ever create a `ClientPackage`, or only an `Invoice`/`InvoiceLine` with no wallet credit? This matters because the business says they sold one "Duo Private" package that isn't in their public product catalog — find out whether it's even possible today to grant package credits for something with no matching Product.

   - `db.Products.find({})` — list all Products, note ones related to "Private" and their Type/Format/price/credits fields, so we see the real catalog.
   - `db.ClientPackages.find({Format: /private/i})` or similar — find any existing PRIVATE-format packages to see real-world field values.
   - Search Invoices/InvoiceLines for anything mentioning "Duo" (grep the JSON via mongosh, e.g. `db.InvoiceLines.find({ProductNameSnapshot: /duo/i})` or similar field names — check actual field names first) to find how the one real Duo Private sale was actually recorded. Report exactly what you find (or that nothing matches, tried strings X/Y/Z).

5. **WalletController** (`wallet` route) — admin manual package grant (`grant-package` endpoint) — how does staff manually assign a package to a client outside of a Product purchase? Does this bypass the Product/PackageBlueprint entirely (i.e., could this be how the one Duo sale is currently sitting in the client's wallet)?

Report back structured with file:line citations, short verbatim code quotes, and the actual query results from prod (redact nothing sensitive like customer PII beyond what's needed — names/amounts are fine, this is the business's own data being reviewed by the business owner). This report will be read by someone designing how to formally support a "Duo Private" package product, so be precise about what's possible today vs. not.

All paths read on `/opt/soulpilates` (live host `51.79.226.200`). Ignore `/opt/soulpilates/backups*`, `/opt/soulpilates/backup-2026-06-30-*`, `/opt/soulpilates/_preupdate_backups` — those are stale snapshots, not the live tree.

## 1. WalletService.cs (`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/WalletService.cs`, 700 lines, read in full)

**The matching key is `ClientId + Format` string only.** No product id, blueprint id, or price is ever part of the wallet lookup.

**`GetActivePackagesForClientAsync(clientId, format)`** — WalletService.cs:73-117 — this is the "active-package resolution by client + format" method:
```csharp
// WalletService.cs:85-98
var upper = (format ?? "").ToUpperInvariant();
var formatFilter = upper == "MAT"
    ? Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.In(p => p.Format, new[] { "MAT", "GROUP" })
    : Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.Eq(p => p.Format, upper == "" ? format : upper);

var filter = Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.And(
    Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.Eq(p => p.ClientId, clientId),
    formatFilter,
    Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.In(p => p.Status, new[] { "ACTIVE", "LOW_BALANCE" }),
    Builders<ClientPackage>.Filter.Gt(p => p.CreditsRemaining, 0),
    expiryOk
);
```
Only `MAT` gets a fallback bucket (`MAT` packages preferred, `GROUP` packages as fallback, sorted MAT-first then by expiry). Everything else — including `PRIVATE`, `DUO`, `FREELANCE` — is a **strict equality match on `Format`**. Sort is FIFO by `ExpiryDate` (nulls last).

**`DeductCreditAsync(string clientId, string format, string referenceAttendanceId, int quantity = 1)`** — WalletService.cs:154-189. Signature confirmed exact. It calls `GetActivePackagesForClientAsync(clientId, format)`, sums `CreditsRemaining`, bails (`return false`, no partial deduction) if `totalAvailable < quantity`, then walks the FIFO-sorted list deducting `Math.Min(pkg.CreditsRemaining, remainingToDeduct)` per wallet, writing one `PackageLedgerLog` (`ActionType = "DEDUCTION"`) per wallet touched, tagged with `referenceAttendanceId`. **So a multi-seat/duo deduction can legitimately span two different `ClientPackage` documents of the same client+format**, reconciled later purely through ledger rows keyed by `ReferenceAttendanceId`.

**Refund/forfeit paths** (`RefundCreditAsync`, `RefundCreditByAttendanceWithTrailAsync` WalletService.cs:236-289, `RefundPartialCreditByAttendanceWithTrailAsync` WalletService.cs:297-341, `ForfeitCreditByAttendanceAsync` WalletService.cs:350-396) **do not re-key off Format at all** — they key off `PackageInstanceId` (found via the `PackageLedgerLog.ReferenceAttendanceId` trail), i.e. they reverse exactly the wallet(s) the original deduction touched, format-agnostic by that point. Format only matters at the initial deduction/wallet-selection step.

## 2. Booking → WalletService call sites (format always comes straight from `CalendarSession.Format`)

There is no single `BookClientAsync` that deducts — `BookClientAsync` (SchedulingService.cs:822-863, admin credit-book) just creates the `Attendance` row with a caller-supplied `packageInstanceId` and does **not** call `DeductCreditAsync` itself. The actual deduction happens in these call sites, and in every one `format` is `session.Format` verbatim (uppercase already, since `CalendarSession.Format` is stored upper-case):

| Call site | file:line | quantity source |
|---|---|---|
| `PaymentService.CreateIntentAsync` (online booking confirm, PACKAGE_CREDIT) | PaymentService.cs:423-428 | `Math.Max(1, attendance.Quantity)` |
| `SchedulingService.SettleBookingWithCreditAsync` (SPM-124, POS settle-with-credit) | SchedulingService.cs:1448-1449 | `Math.Max(1, attendance.Quantity)` |
| `SchedulingService.WalkInCheckoutAsync` (POS walk-in) | SchedulingService.cs:1568 | implicit 1 |
| `SchedulingService.AdjustAttendeeQuantityAsync` (grow an existing booking) | SchedulingService.cs:2878-2879 | `delta` seats |

Example (PaymentService.cs:405-428):
```csharp
var activeWallets = (await _walletService
    .GetActivePackagesForClientAsync(attendance.ClientId, session.Format))
    .ToList();
...
var deducted = await _walletService.DeductCreditAsync(
    attendance.ClientId, session.Format, attendanceId, quantityNeeded);
```
`CalendarSession.Format` is snapshotted from `ClassBlueprint.Format` when the session is materialized (SchedulingService.cs:3647, 3673, 3821, 3869: `.Set(s => s.Format, blueprint.Format)` / `session.Format = bp.Format`). So the answer to "is Format derived from the blueprint/session directly" is **yes, unconditionally** — no other dimension enters the wallet lookup.

`Attendance.Quantity` (Attendance.cs:77, default 1) is the seats-per-row field; a duo booking is **one Attendance row with Quantity=2**, not two rows (see §3).

## 3. Private/Duo pricing — an existing "Duo Class" feature already covers this exact scenario

This is the big finding: **Soul Pilates already has a "Duo Private" concept** (ticket tag `SPM-98`, "Make it a Duo Class"), and it is implemented as a **headcount-based price override**, not a separate package/product type.

**`GlobalSettings.PrivateDuoPrice`** — `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/Entities/GlobalSettings.cs:116`:
```csharp
/// <summary>Flat price for a PRIVATE Duo Class (2 people). When > 0, a private
/// session booked for 2 bills this instead of 2x the drop-in. Cash/online only —
/// credit bookings still cost 2 credits. Defaults to 1,300,000 VND.</summary>
public decimal PrivateDuoPrice { get; set; } = 1_300_000m;
```
This is the literal `1,300,000` you asked about. **No `850,000` literal exists anywhere in the repo** (API/Services/Core/Astro grepped — zero hits).

**`PaymentService.DuoAwareTotal`** — PaymentService.cs:143-148 — the headcount-based price branch:
```csharp
public static decimal DuoAwareTotal(string? format, decimal dropIn, int seats, decimal privateDuoPrice)
{
    if (seats < 1) seats = 1;
    if (format == "PRIVATE" && seats == 2 && privateDuoPrice > 0m) return privateDuoPrice;
    return dropIn * seats;
}
```
Called from `PaymentService.QuotePriceAsync` (PaymentService.cs:186, non-package cash/Stripe quoting) and from `SchedulingService` at SchedulingService.cs:1164 and :1189 (recomputing amount-due on POS collect / balance checks). **This is the exact headcount-price-multiplier logic you were asked to search for.**

Important asymmetry already in the code (relevant to your design):
- **PACKAGE_CREDIT bookings are NOT duo-aware on price** — the comment says "credit bookings still cost 2 credits" (flat 2, not a discounted duo rate) — `DeductCreditAsync(..., quantity: 2)` just takes 2 credits from the ordinary `PRIVATE` wallet.
- **The admin/desk "add attendee" path does NOT use `DuoAwareTotal`** — `AdminAddStudentAsync`-style flow at SchedulingService.cs:2585 computes `amountDue = (session.DropInPrice ?? 0m) * requestedSeats`, i.e. plain 2× drop-in, not the flat duo price. So today there's already a pricing inconsistency between the online/POS-collect duo quote (flat 1.3M) and the desk-add duo booking (2× drop-in) — worth knowing before adding a third "Duo Private" package type.

**How "duo" is represented on a booking** — there is **no boolean/enum "DUO" field on Attendance**. It's inferred purely as `session.Format == "PRIVATE" && Quantity == 2`:
- Frontend: `checkout.astro` — `isDuoBooking() { return session?.format === "PRIVATE" && intent?.duo === true; }` (checkout.astro:2081-2084), locks `quantity = 2` client-side.
- Backend: `SchedulingService.ReserveSpotAsync` (SchedulingService.cs:1877-1907) — a `PRIVATE`-format session normally has `Capacity = 1`; on a 2-seat request from a solo booker it bumps `session.Capacity` to 2 for that one session and stores `Quantity = 2` on the single `Attendance` row. Same capacity-bump pattern repeated in the admin add-attendee path (SchedulingService.cs:2549-2568) and the quantity-adjust path (SchedulingService.cs:2830-2860), all guarded by a `BOOKING.PRIVATE_DUO_MAX` business rule capping a PRIVATE session at 2 total seats.

Separately, there is also a literal **`"DUO"`** format string used in a few places (`CalendarSession.Format` comment at CalendarSession.cs:36 lists `"GROUP","MAT","PRIVATE","DUO"`; dev seed data at `DevSeedController.cs:80` creates sessions with `Format = "DUO"` and `Capacity = 2`). This is a **separate, largely legacy/analytics-only concept** from the SPM-98 "Duo Class" feature — real duo bookings created via the booking flow keep `session.Format == "PRIVATE"` (never actually set to `"DUO"`) and instead bump `Capacity` and `Quantity`. The `"DUO"` format string is only consumed for: display labels (SchedulingService.cs:3131: `"DUO" => "Duo Private Session"`), analytics bucketing (`AnalyticsService.cs:2253`: `"DUO" => "PRIVATE"` — folds DUO-format sessions into the PRIVATE revenue/credit bucket for reporting), and a couple of `Format == "PRIVATE" || Format == "DUO"` OR-checks in analytics/payroll. **Crucially, `WalletService.GetActivePackagesForClientAsync` does NOT special-case `"DUO"` the way it special-cases `"MAT"→GROUP`** — a `ClientPackage.Format == "DUO"` package would only match a session literally formatted `"DUO"`, and since real duo bookings never set `session.Format = "DUO"`, such a wallet would currently be unreachable from the real booking flow. Any "Duo Private" package design needs to either (a) reuse `Format == "PRIVATE"` and gate on `Quantity == 2` the way pricing already does, or (b) if it wants a distinct `Format == "DUO"` wallet bucket, add an analogous fallback/alias rule to `GetActivePackagesForClientAsync` (mirroring the existing MAT→GROUP pattern) — otherwise it will silently never be found.

## 4. PayrollService — headcount counting confirmed to be per-SEAT (sums `Quantity`), not per-attendance-row

`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/PayrollService.cs`, the `FIXED_HEADCOUNT` tier-resolution loop (SchedulingService's sibling), private branch at PayrollService.cs:462-468:
```csharp
// PayrollService.cs:411-419 (group) / :462-468 (private, same pattern)
// SPM-90 — the headcount ladder is per SEAT, not per attendance
// ROW. A group booking of N seats (att.Quantity == N) counts as
// N students...
var seatHeadcount = arrivedAttendances
    .Where(a => a.CountsTowardsCommission)
    .Sum(a => Math.Max(1, a.Quantity));

result.PrivateClassEarnings += ResolveHeadcountPayoutFromSnapshot(result, seatHeadcount, isPrivate: true);
```
So **yes** — a 2-person duo private represented as one `Attendance` row with `Quantity = 2` (which is how the current SPM-98 duo flow actually stores it — confirmed §3) is correctly counted as `seatHeadcount = 2` and would correctly hit `Staff.PrivateHeadcountTiers`' 2-person tier. If instead you represent a future "Duo Private" as **two separate Attendance rows** (one per client) each with `Quantity = 1`, that also sums to 2 correctly — the `.Sum(a => Math.Max(1, a.Quantity))` is row-count-agnostic, it just needs `CountsTowardsCommission == true` on each row and both counted as `arrivedAttendances` (i.e. `IsAttendancePaidAsync` true) on the same `CalendarSession`.

One thing to flag: the branch selector `isPrivate` used for this normal per-session compute loop is narrower than the `isPrivateFmt` used for the override/imported-commission short-circuits earlier in the same method:
```csharp
// PayrollService.cs:364 — used for CommissionOverride / imported-commission short-circuits
var isPrivateFmt = session.Capacity == 1 || session.Format == "PRIVATE" || session.Format == "DUO";
...
// PayrollService.cs:398 — used for the normal FIXED_HEADCOUNT/PERCENTAGE_TIERED compute path
var isPrivate = session.Capacity == 1 || session.Format == "PRIVATE";
```
`isPrivate` (no `"DUO"`) is what actually drives which headcount-tier ladder (`PrivateHeadcountTiersSnapshot` vs `HeadcountTiersSnapshot`) gets used for the bulk of sessions. A session whose `Format` is literally `"DUO"` (not `"PRIVATE"`) would fall through to the **GROUP** commission ladder in the normal path despite being flagged private in the override/imported paths — an existing inconsistency. This doesn't affect the real SPM-98 duo flow (which keeps `Format == "PRIVATE"`), but it's a landmine if a new "Duo Private" package/session type is implemented using a distinct `Format == "DUO"` value rather than reusing `"PRIVATE"` + `Quantity`.

## 5. All `GetActivePackage*` / package-resolution call sites (repo-wide grep, `select:` — no `ResolvePackage`/`MatchingPackage` names exist anywhere)

- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/Interfaces/IWalletService.cs:10` — interface declaration
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/WalletService.cs:73` (definition), `:158` (used internally by `DeductCreditAsync`)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/PaymentService.cs:405` — `CreateIntentAsync` pre-flight (§2)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs:1439` — `SettleBookingWithCreditAsync`
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs:1556` — `WalkInCheckoutAsync` auto-match
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs:244-245` — client-portal wallet summary (GROUP + PRIVATE, separately)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs:336` — `ReserveSpotAsync` auto-match by `session.Format`
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs:452-454` — another wallet-summary read (GROUP, PRIVATE, MAT)
- `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.API/Controllers/BookingController.cs:534` — another `session.Format` auto-match

All nine call sites pass either a hardcoded literal (`"GROUP"`, `"PRIVATE"`, `"MAT"`) for summary/wallet-display purposes, or `session.Format` for an actual booking-time lookup. None pass a product id, blueprint id, or price — `ClientId + Format` (string) is the sole matching key throughout the whole codebase, confirmed with no exceptions.

*(Adjacent but unrelated: `SchedulingService.ResolveFreelancePackageIdAsync` at SchedulingService.cs:4184-4218 does its own separate `ClientId + Format` filter directly against the `ClientPackages` collection for the Studio-Rentals/freelance-instructor feature — same pattern, different consumer, not part of the customer booking path.)*</result>

## 3. Private/Duo pricing — an existing "Duo Class" feature already covers this exact scenario

This is the big finding: **Soul Pilates already has a "Duo Private" concept** (ticket tag `SPM-98`, "Make it a Duo Class"), and it is implemented as a **headcount-based price override**, not a separate package/product type.

**`GlobalSettings.PrivateDuoPrice`** — `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Core/Entities/GlobalSettings.cs:116`:

```csharp
{
```

Important asymmetry already in the code (relevant to your design):
- **PACKAGE_CREDIT bookings are NOT duo-aware on price** — the comment says "credit bookings still cost 2 credits" (flat 2, not a discounted duo rate) — `DeductCreditAsync(..., quantity: 2)` just takes 2 credits from the ordinary `PRIVATE` wallet.

So today there's already a pricing inconsistency between the online/POS-collect duo quote (flat 1.3M) and the desk-add duo booking (2× drop-in) — worth knowing before adding a third "Duo Private" package type.

**How "duo" is represented on a booking** — there is **no boolean/enum "DUO" field on Attendance**. It's inferred purely as `session.Format == "PRIVATE" && Quantity == 2`:
- Frontend: `checkout.astro` — `isDuoBooking() { return session?.format === "PRIVATE" && intent?.duo === true; }` (checkout.astro:2081-2084), locks `quantity = 2` client-side.
- Backend: `SchedulingService.ReserveSpotAsync` (SchedulingService.cs:1877-1907) — a `PRIVATE`-format session normally has `Capacity = 1`; on a 2-seat request from a solo booker it bumps `session.Capacity` to 2 for that one session and stores `Quantity = 2` on the single `Attendance` row. Separately, there is also a literal **`"DUO"`** format string used in a few places (`CalendarSession.Format` comment at CalendarSession.cs:36 lists `"GROUP","MAT","PRIVATE","DUO"`; dev seed data at `DevSeedController.cs:80` creates sessions with `Format = "DUO"` and `Capacity = 2`). Any "Duo Private" package design needs to either (a) reuse `Format == "PRIVATE"` and gate on `Quantity == 2` the way pricing already does, or (b) if it wants a distinct `Format == "DUO"` wallet bucket, add an analogous fallback/alias rule to `GetActivePackagesForClientAsync` (mirroring the existing MAT→GROUP pattern) — otherwise it will silently never be found.

## 4. PayrollService — headcount counting confirmed to be per-SEAT (sums `Quantity`), not per-attendance-row

`/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Services/PayrollService.cs`, the `FIXED_HEADCOUNT` tier-resolution loop (SchedulingService's sibling), private branch at PayrollService.cs:462-468:

```csharp
    .Where(a => a.CountsTowardsCommission)
```

So **yes** — a 2-person duo private represented as one `Attendance` row with `Quantity = 2` (which is how the current SPM-98 duo flow actually stores it — confirmed §3) is correctly counted as `seatHeadcount = 2` and would correctly hit `Staff.PrivateHeadcountTiers`' 2-person tier. ...

### How PRIVATE-format `Capacity` is actually set/bumped

There is **extensive, deliberate special-casing of PRIVATE format capacity** in `SchedulingService.cs`, all under ticket **SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class"**:

- A `PRIVATE` blueprint/session is normally created with `Capacity = 1` (a 1-on-1 slot) — this is asserted directly in several comments, e.g. `SchedulingService.cs:1882`: *"A PRIVATE session is created with Capacity=1, so for the duo case we bump the session's effective capacity to 2 to make room for the second seat."*
- **`ReserveSpotAsync` (public booking path), `SchedulingService.cs:1877-1902`:**
  ```csharp
  // SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class" — a PRIVATE session may be booked as a
  // duo (2 seats) by a single booker who covers both seats. We mirror the
  // existing DUO format (capacity 2): the booker's single attendance carries
  // Quantity=2, CurrentBookings is incremented by 2, and 2 credits / 2× the
  // drop-in are charged via the same multi-seat path GROUP bookings use.
  // A PRIVATE session is created with Capacity=1, so for the duo case we bump
  // the session's effective capacity to 2 to make room for the second seat.
  // Anything other than the 1-seat or duo (2-seat) case on a PRIVATE session
  // is clamped to 1 so a malicious payload can't over-book a 1-to-1 class.
  if (session.Format == "PRIVATE")
  {
      var othersBooked = session.CurrentBookings - (existingReserved?.Quantity ?? 0);
      if (quantity == 2 && othersBooked <= 0)
      {
          if (session.Capacity < 2)
          {
              await _sessions.UpdateOneAsync(s => s.Id == sessionId,
                  Builders<CalendarSession>.Update.Set(s => s.Capacity, 2));
              session.Capacity = 2;
          }
      }
      else { quantity = 1; }
  }
  ```
- **`AdminAddStudentAsync` (desk/admin add path), `SchedulingService.cs:2532-2568`:** clamps requested seats to a max of 2 on `PRIVATE`, throws `BOOKING.PRIVATE_DUO_MAX` if the total would exceed 2, and bumps `Capacity` to 2 only when needed.
- **`AdjustAttendeeQuantityAsync`, `SchedulingService.cs:2849-2861`:** same bump-to-2 logic when growing an existing PRIVATE booking from 1→2 seats.
- **`RestorePrivateCapacityIfEmptyAsync`, `SchedulingService.cs:2096-2110`:** shrinks `Capacity` back from 2→1 once no active seats remain, so a freed 1-on-1 slot can't later be double-booked by two unrelated singles. Guard: `if (session.Format != "PRIVATE" || session.Capacity <= 1) return;`
- Hard cap enforced everywhere: **a PRIVATE session can never hold more than 2 people** (`BOOKING.PRIVATE_DUO_MAX`, e.g. `SchedulingService.cs:2562-2563,2832-2833,2856-2857`).
- Reschedule (`RescheduleBookingAsync`, ~line 3002) requires `originalSession.Format == newSession.Format` (`BOOKING.FORMAT_MISMATCH`), and moves the full `attendance.Quantity` (duo=2, group=N) to the new session (comment at line 3007).

So: **Capacity is normally 1 for PRIVATE, and yes, it does get bumped to 2** — but only dynamically at booking time, never by the blueprint/materialiser. This is the live "Duo Private" mechanism.

### `Quantity` — the key answer

The doc comment on `Quantity` (`Attendance.cs:68-77`) is itself **out of date / contradicted by the actual SPM-98 code**:
```csharp
/// Number of seats this attendance row represents. Group-class only —
/// private classes are always 1. Defaults to 1 so legacy rows deserialise unchanged.
public int Quantity { get; set; } = 1;
```
Despite saying "private classes are always 1," `SchedulingService.cs` explicitly sets `Quantity = 2` on a single `Attendance` row for a duo booking on a PRIVATE session (SPM-98):

- `SplitBookingAsync`, `SchedulingService.cs:2792-2831`: can split a multi-seat (e.g. duo) attendance back into two single-seat `Attendance` rows.

**So `Quantity` is used today to represent "this one booking is for N people," and that mechanism is exactly how a duo private booking is currently modeled** — one `Attendance` row, `Quantity=2`, rather than two separate rows (although `SplitBookingAsync` supports converting it into two separate rows on demand). This is the load-bearing mechanism for "Duo Private" as it exists in the live system.

`PayrollService.cs:364` and `AnalyticsService.cs` (`Format == "PRIVATE" || Format == "DUO"`) both special-case private-style formats when reasoning about commission/occupancy, since a `Quantity=2` "PRIVATE" duo attendance is functionally different from a normal 1-seat private session.

### How PRIVATE-format `Capacity` is actually set/bumped

There is **extensive, deliberate special-casing of PRIVATE format capacity** in `SchedulingService.cs`, all under ticket **SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class"**:

- A `PRIVATE` blueprint/session is normally created with `Capacity = 1` (a 1-on-1 slot) — this is asserted directly in several comments, e.g. `SchedulingService.cs:1882`: *"A PRIVATE session is created with Capacity=1, so for the duo case we bump the session's effective capacity to 2 to make room for the second seat."*
- **`ReserveSpotAsync` (public booking path), `SchedulingService.cs:1877-1902`:**
  ```csharp
  // SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class" — a PRIVATE session may be booked as a
  // duo (2 seats) by a single booker who covers both seats. We mirror the
  // existing DUO format (capacity 2): the booker's single attendance carries
  // Quantity=2, CurrentBookings is incremented by 2, and 2 credits / 2× the
  // drop-in are charged via the same multi-seat path GROUP bookings use.
  // A PRIVATE session is created with Capacity=1, so for the duo case we bump
  // the session's effective capacity to 2 to make room for the second seat.
  // Anything other than the 1-seat or duo (2-seat) case on a PRIVATE session
  // is clamped to 1 so a malicious payload can't over-book a 1-to-1 class.
  if (session.Format == "PRIVATE")
  {
      var othersBooked = session.CurrentBookings - (existingReserved?.Quantity ?? 0);
      if (quantity == 2 && othersBooked <= 0)
      {
          if (session.Capacity < 2)
          {
              await _sessions.UpdateOneAsync(s => s.Id == sessionId,
                  Builders<CalendarSession>.Update.Set(s => s.Capacity, 2));
              session.Capacity = 2;
          }
      }
      else { quantity = 1; }
  }
  ```
- **`AdminAddStudentAsync` (desk/admin add path), `SchedulingService.cs:2532-2568`:** clamps requested seats to a max of 2 on `PRIVATE`, throws `BOOKING.PRIVATE_DUO_MAX` if the total would exceed 2, and bumps `Capacity` to 2 only when needed.
- **`AdjustAttendeeQuantityAsync`, `SchedulingService.cs:2849-2861`:** same bump-to-2 logic when growing an existing PRIVATE booking from 1→2 seats.
- **`RestorePrivateCapacityIfEmptyAsync`, `SchedulingService.cs:2096-2110`:** shrinks `Capacity` back from 2→1 once no active seats remain, so a freed 1-on-1 slot can't later be double-booked by two unrelated singles. Guard: `if (session.Format != "PRIVATE" || session.Capacity <= 1) return;`
- Hard cap enforced everywhere: **a PRIVATE session can never hold more than 2 people** (`BOOKING.PRIVATE_DUO_MAX`, e.g. `SchedulingService.cs:2562-2563,2832-2833,2856-2857`).
- Reschedule (`RescheduleBookingAsync`, ~line 3002) requires `originalSession.Format == newSession.Format` (`BOOKING.FORMAT_MISMATCH`), and moves the full `attendance.Quantity` (duo=2, group=N) to the new session (comment at line 3007).

So: **Capacity is normally 1 for PRIVATE, and yes, it does get bumped to 2** — but only dynamically at booking time, never by the blueprint/materialiser. This is the live "Duo Private" mechanism.

**`SoulPilates.Services/SchedulingService.cs:1833` `ReserveSpotAsync`**, lines ~1876–1907, is where the duo case is special-cased:
```csharp
// SPM-98 "Make it a Duo Class" — a PRIVATE session may be booked as a
// duo (2 seats) by a single booker who covers both seats. We mirror the
// existing DUO format (capacity 2): the booker's single attendance carries
// Quantity=2, CurrentBookings is incremented by 2, and 2 credits / 2× the
// drop-in are charged via the same multi-seat path GROUP bookings use.
if (session.Format == "PRIVATE")
{
    var othersBooked = session.CurrentBookings - (existingReserved?.Quantity ?? 0);
    if (quantity == 2 && othersBooked <= 0)
    {
        if (session.Capacity < 2) { /* bump session.Capacity to 2 */ }
    }
    else { quantity = 1; }
}
```
**There is no durable "this was a duo booking" marker anywhere.** `Attendance.Quantity` (`SoulPilates.Core/Entities/Attendance.cs:77`) is the only signal — a PRIVATE-format attendance with `Quantity == 2` *is* the duo, inferred after the fact by re-checking `format == "PRIVATE" && seats == 2` (as `PaymentService.DuoAwareTotal` and `SchedulingService.cs:1164/1189` both do). No `IsDuo` boolean, no `BookingType` enum, nothing stored that says "this is a Duo Class" as opposed to "customer happened to book 2 seats of a session whose capacity was bumped to 2." If a future PRIVATE session legitimately had 2 unrelated people book 1 seat each (not possible today since capacity is 1 unless bumped by this exact code path, but worth flagging as a fragile inference), the marker would be ambiguous.

Credit deduction for a duo booking on check-in also comes from a client's **PRIVATE**-format package (not a distinct "DUO" package) — `WalletService.GetActivePackagesForClientAsync(clientId, format)` (`WalletService.cs:73-92`) does exact-match on `ClientPackage.Format == session.Format`, and `session.Format` stays `"PRIVATE"` throughout the SPM-98 duo flow (only `Quantity`/`Capacity` change), so 2 credits are drawn from a regular Private package, not any duo-specific package.

### 3. `my-package.astro` — client wallet view

**File:** `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/my-package.astro`

- Format filter chips (lines 61–69) only offer **All / Group / Private** — no DUO chip exists:

- Format is rendered **raw/uppercase, untranslated** in `packageRowItem()` (lines 752–768):
```js

const fmtColor = fmt === "PRIVATE" ? "#f59e0b" : "#6366f1";
...
<span class="sp-pkg-format-tag">
```

So today a client sees literally `PRIVATE` or `GROUP` as the tag text — no friendly label map exists here (unlike `admin/products.astro`, see #5). A `DUO`-format package would render the raw string `"DUO"` with the same indigo dot color as `GROUP` (the ternary only special-cases `PRIVATE`), i.e. **visually indistinguishable from a Group package today** — this is a concrete gap if a "Duo Private" package needs to stand out.

- Fields shown per package (lines 726–834): `creditsRemaining`/`totalCredits`/`creditsUsed`, `expiryDate` (or blank for open-ended, per SPM-121 comment at line 746-751), `activationDate`, `status` (via `statusLabel()`, line 842), and a short package ID chip.

**File:** `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/client-profile.astro`

- Package cards render **`w.productName ?? "Package"`** (line 707) — i.e., admin sees the Product's configured name (e.g. "Group 10-Class Pack"), not the raw `Format` — different behavior from `my-package.astro`. So on the admin side, naming a product "Duo Private 5-Class Pack" would already surface correctly without any format-label engineering.
- "Add package" is a **direct comp grant, not a purchase** ("Add Package (Comp Grant)" modal, lines 376–418, comment at 376: *"direct comp grant, no invoice/revenue"*). Staff pick a Product from a dropdown populated from `GET /api/product` filtered to `type === 'PACKAGE' && isActive !== false` (lines 1176–1201):

```js
return `<option value="${p.id}">${p.name} — ${fmt}${credits} credits · ${validity}</option>`;
```

This confirms the product's `formatRestriction` (e.g. `PRIVATE`, `DUO`) is shown in the dropdown label. Submission goes to `POST /api/wallet/client/${clientId}/grant-package` (line ~1240) with a required audit-log `reason`.

### 5. Admin `products.astro` / `product-form.astro` — already supports a "DUO" format product today

**File:** `/opt/soulpilates/SoulPilates.Astro/src/pages/admin/product-form.astro`

The Format `<select>` **already has a `DUO` option** (lines 68–74):
```html

    <option value="GROUP">Group</option>
```

It's disabled/hidden only for studio-rental product types (lines 519–546):
```js

}
if (isStudioRental && formatSelect.value === "DUO") {
  formatSelect.value = "GROUP";
```
